short_description: A drug eruption is a skin reaction that can happen after taking a medication. It may appear as a rash, redness, itching, swelling, or blisters. Some reactions are mild, but others can be serious and need urgent medical attention.

low: small red spots without other symptoms
high: rash after starting a new medication

temporary_advice: Do not take another dose until you get medical advice if you suspect a medication reaction
Write down the name of the medication and when symptoms started
Keep the skin cool and avoid harsh products
Seek medical advice quickly if the rash spreads or swelling appears
avoid: Do not ignore swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or difficulty breathing
Do not restart the suspected medication without medical advice
Avoid mixing medicines without consulting a doctor or pharmacist
Avoid applying random creams on a severe rash
risk_notes: Drug reactions can be mild, but some can become urgent, especially if there is breathing difficulty, facial swelling, fever, blisters, or skin peeling.
when_to_see_doctor: Urgently if there is difficulty breathing or swelling of face/lips/tongue
Urgently if rash appears with fever, blisters, or skin peeling
If the rash started after a new medication
If symptoms spread quickly or become painful
If you are unsure whether to continue the medication
